top.line: A book site built in one evening
top.para: Between 21:27 on 18 October and 04:33 the next morning, a team of agents with roles, many in parallel, built gen-z-developers.sgit.ai from Dinis's memos: the 2018 edition rebuilt exactly, two frozen release candidates from 198 traced ideas, a graph, storyboards, infographics, covers, decisions and synthetic readers. The book's positioning appeared only after the first draft.

in-short.line: Thirty-seven releases, and a book discovered
in-short.para: An empty repository became site v0.2.33 in one evening. The first edition was rebuilt exactly; the new one reached two release candidates, the second at 41 chapters and 73,314 words. Roles worked in parallel. Synthetic readers would not buy it yet. And the startup positioning came after the first draft, which is how the book is being discovered.

evening.line: From an empty repository to v0.2.33
evening.para: After six articles and two build briefs on 18 October, the repository was empty at 21:27 London time. The first release, built from them, went out at 21:55; the thirty-seventh, v0.2.33, at 04:33. In between: 58 commits, each release with a note saying what changed and why, and six working branches, most of them a role working on its own.

built.para: The 2018 edition as v1.0.0, with its print PDF matched page by page; two frozen release candidates, the second 41 chapters from 198 ideas, with 47 notes for Dinis; a reader with the newsroom's meter and the chapter's graph; the book as a graph of 857 nodes; twelve storyboards, 81 proposed infographics and three covers in every format Amazon and Leanpub take.

players.line: A team with roles, and Dinis
players.para: A journalist turns memos into articles that brief the roles; a librarian keeps the book as a graph; an editor interviews Dinis and owns the readers; a reviewer judges the 2018 text; a publisher ships; a review board argues each change; seven writers draft chapters; an illustrator and designer, with an art director. The agents sign nine articles of their own.

workflow.line: Memo, article, ideas, chapters, candidate, decision
workflow.para: Dinis records a memo; the journalist writes it up as an article with a brief; the librarian turns it into traced ideas on a chapter map; writers draft chapters only from those ideas; the candidate is frozen for Dinis to read and mark; decisions are recorded in his words. Many steps ran at once on separate branches.

discovered.line: The positioning came after the first draft
discovered.para: Release candidate 1 was built at 01:47 as Gen Z Developers (GenAI Edition). Four minutes later a memo recorded after seeing it proposed the founder as the reader: Generation ZX Developers, for Generation Z and X, ending with a company started. It was decision 014 at 02:06, and rc2 was rewritten under it by 02:46. Seeing the draft made the question possible.

worked.para: Frozen candidates read and diffed; provenance enforced by the build, for chapters and for readers' quotes; decisions in Dinis's words; agents accounting for their own work; synthetic readers honest enough to say they would not buy it yet; and reuse of the newsroom's meter, themes, version history, synthetic-users method and review records.

open.para: Forty-seven notes wait on Dinis, above all how readers report the companies they start and the chapters on forming a company in the UK, Lithuania, Portugal and the EU. Readers found repetition in the hands-on part and the co-writing mentioned only at the end. Edition or new book is undecided, and the cover's seven or eight lines need checking.

limits.para: Nothing in the new edition is signed off. The readers are invented and played by a model, not reader research. The times are commit times converted to London time. And volume is not quality: the readers' verdict is the measure, and it is not yet a yes.

sources.line: The site, its repository and a memo
sources.para: From Dinis's memo of 19 October 2026, gen-z-developers.sgit.ai at v0.2.33 with its release history, decisions, release candidate and synthetic readers, its repository's commits and branches, and screenshots of the live site taken that day.
